set.approach: From the highway, a hiking trail leads in through the woods toward the wall of south-facing flows; reaching the area can involve crossing a beaver dam, and the climbs appear off to the left. Aurora Borealis is roughly the second or third flow along the wall, and the trail brings you straight to its base.

review.notes: Route page for the flow position and trail; area page for the trail and beaver dam. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start from the pull-out for the Awausee hiking trail beside the highway and follow the trail back until the upper pillars come into view. Turn left there and go up the snow gullies to the base, before the trail drops away. Snowshoes make the walk in much easier when the snow is deep.

review.notes: Route page for the trail and turn-off; area page agrees the walk is a woodland hike from the highway. Descent text on the page is garbled, so none written.

set.approach: A hikers' trail runs close to the highway; follow it in through the woods and across a beaver dam, and the south-facing ice climbs on the east side of the road appear off to the left.
set.descent_text: Parties rappel back down the route itself from the tree or screw belays.

review.notes: Route page says to rappel the route; approach is area-level only.

set.approach: Take the hiking trail in from the highway through the woods; the climbs show up to the left after a beaver dam crossing. M.E.T. lies on the Panama Wall ice crag, a short way west (climber's left) of Aurora Borealis.

review.notes: Route page for position relative to Aurora Borealis; area page for the trail. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the hiking trail in from the highway through the woods; the climbs show up to the left after a beaver dam crossing. Three Avengers fills a steep, rocky crevice a short way to the right of Aurora Borealis, and it sits in more shade than its neighbour.

review.notes: Route page for position and character; area page for the trail. No descent stated.

set.approach: The route is in the gully between the second and third rock buttresses of the canyon, low in the gully, on its left-hand side. The second buttress is just past the camp and the bend in the canyon road, with a deep left-facing gash on its left side.
set.descent_text: Descend by building a V-thread, or by wrapping a pillar for the rappel.

review.notes: Route page for location and descent; area page for the buttress position.

set.approach: The ice sits in a cirque higher up and east of the Colossus Wall crag. Follow the approach to that wall, then go up the gully to its right, trending left into the cirque. The route is on the lower right part of the main wall.
set.descent_text: Climb the right side of the curtain of ice and walk off to the left.

review.notes: Route page for walk-off and position; area page for the cirque approach. Single source for descent.

set.approach: The ice sits in a cirque higher up and east of the Colossus Wall crag. Follow the approach to that wall, then go up the gully to its right, trending left into the cirque. The line runs up the gully's left-hand side just where it widens into the cirque.

review.notes: Route page for position; area page for the cirque approach. No descent stated.

set.approach: The ice sits in a cirque higher up and east of the Colossus Wall crag. Follow the approach to that wall, then go up the gully to its right, trending left into the cirque. It follows a big corner that faces right, on the left part of the main wall.
set.descent_text: Descend by V-thread if the ice is thick enough, and carry rock gear in case it is not.

review.notes: Route page for location and descent; area page for the cirque approach.

set.approach: Drive up the canyon past the camp and the Terminal Cancer couloir comes into view on the right. Park along the road near the wall, cross the river at any convenient spot and head up the slope; the road is sometimes not cleared all the way in winter, so you may need to walk or skin up it. The ice is a few hundred feet left of the couloir, under its large triangular face.
set.descent_text: Either rappel off a V-thread cut a little under the top of the flow, or hike off through the trees on climber's right.

review.notes: Route page for descent and position; area page for parking and river crossing.

set.approach: Park in a roadside pull-off beside Route 100 close to the crag, then walk carefully along the road until the flow appears beside you on the right, then cross over to its base.
set.descent_text: Walk up around the left side to the trees above, where the anchor is, and lower off from there.

review.notes: Both pages agree on the walk around climber's left to tree anchors.

set.approach: Park at the pull-off for this section of the gulf and walk south along the road, watching for traffic. Where the river bends behind some trees, cross it and climb the hillside; the ice is visible once you reach the river. Take care on the river ice, and gaiters help if you get wet.
set.descent_text: A tree anchor at the top allows a walk-off.

review.notes: Route page for approach and walk-off; area page for the parking and roadside walk.

set.approach: Park at the pull-out just north of the falls and take the short trail in. It is the showpiece flow of the gulf and can be seen from Route 100.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on parking at the falls. No descent stated.
